segments.text: hey everyone in today's video I'm going
to share with you 11 types of biases
that occur during
sampling sampling bias refers to a
situation in which the sample selected
from a population does not represent
that population leading to erroneous or
misleading
conclusions there are several types of
biases that can occur during the
sampling
process selection bias this happens when
the method of selecting the sample
systematically exclude certain groups or
individuals from the population for
example if a survey is conducted by only
calling landline phone numbers it may
exclude individuals who only have mo
mobile phones leading to selection
bias non response bias this bias occurs
when some individuals chose for the
sample do not respond or participate in
the study if the nonrespondents differ
in some important way from the
respondents the results May not
accurately represent the
population under coverage bias this bias
arises when some groups or elements in
the population are not included or are
inadequately represented in the sample
for for instance if a survey is
conducted during working hours it might
under repesent people who work night
shifts volunteer bias volunteer bias
happens when the sample is composed of
individuals who willingly choose to
participate in a study volunteers may
have different characteristics or
motivation than the general population
leading to a nonrepresentative su ex
Le response bias this bias occurs when
the responses given by participants do
not accurately reflect their true
opinions or behaviors it can be
influenced by factors like social
desirability people giving answers they
think are socially acceptable leading
questions or the order of questions in a
survey survivorship bias this occurs
when the sample includes only the
surviving or successful members of a
population for example if you only study
successful businesses you may miss the
failures which can distort your
understanding of what leads to success
another example patients die during
medical
procedure sampling frame bias this
happens when the list or Source from
which the sample is drone does not
accurately represent the population if
for example a survey of a city's
residence is based on an outdated or
incomplete list of addresses it may not
be
representative temporal bias temporal
bias can occur when the timing of data
collection is not representative or the
population's characteristics over time
for instance if you conduct a survey
about all holay shopping abits in
January the results May not accurately
reflect the behaviors during the holiday
season geographical bias geographical
bias can occur if the sample is not
spread out evenly across a region
leading to over representation or under
representation of certain
areas confirmation bias this is a
cognitive bias that can affect effect
the selection and interpretation of data
researchers May unconsciously seek out
or emphasize information that confirms
their pre-existing beliefs or hypothesis
leading to biased
results instrument bias if the
measurement instruments used in a study
are flowed or biased it can introduced
measurement bias into the
sample for example a FY thermometer

readings has data scientists it's
important to be aware of these biases
